evidence.quote: by my count it should be 1,030
The bankroll on the table reads 1,015

criteria.why: Mostly plain dealer talk with no JSON, but turn 5 talks about the table's own bookkeeping discrepancy, which breaks the dealer voice.

evidence.quote: You check, and the opponent checks behind you.
You fold and forfeit your 10 ante.

criteria.why: Most moves are answered. In turn 1 the player said check or call, and the reply called 5, which was reasonable. Turn 9 correctly refuses the illegal bet and lists the options. Turn 7's fold is acted on, but the pot/bankroll story is off.

evidence.quote: At showdown your K-high straight (K-Q-J-10-9) beats their 9-high, so you win the 30 pot
Dealing a new seven-card stud hand.

criteria.why: The house deals, plays the showdown and settles itself without handing any job to the player. Only the turn 5 mention of a wrong count is a flaw, and that is not a handoff.

The numbers contradict each other. The 30 pot win moved the bankroll 985 to 1,015, and the reply in turn 5 admits a mismatch with 1,030. Hand 2 starts at 1,005 after a 1,015 bankroll, and hand 3 starts at 995 after the fold left it at 1,005, so the bankroll never adds up.
